I checked all 94 fixed rows. **90 fixes are right and 4 need adjusting.** I also adjusted 2 rows outside the 94 to fix the Legacy duplicate. Everything here comes from the CSV columns. I opened no Drive files and edited nothing except the output file.

Output: `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\Flint\.claude\worktrees\step1-triage\data\_tmp\round2_check.csv` (6 adjust rows, written with Python's csv module, header `key,verdict,disciplines,tier,route,candidate,why`).

**Adjusted, by type**

- **Dropped candidate that should be restored (1):** ad48fc49, "Vertical Foundations" (126 pages). The reviewer called it an unknown-author consumer jump ebook. I am fairly sure it is Joel Smith's (Just Fly Sports) jump-training book, which makes it a credible practitioner source for football power work. I set it to B, book, candidate=yes. The author is not in the columns, so confirm it at the shortlist.
- **Candidate kept that should be dropped (1):** 84ba6abb, "2018 Panther Off Site Training Strategies" (160 pages). It is an off-site training packet for one team's athletes. That is program material, not a landmark source. I set it to B, atomize, no. This one is a judgement call.
- **Route fixed because the reviewer's reason was wrong (1):** 4af851e1. The file's original name is "Under the Bar.pdf" (Dave Tate, 144 pages), so the book is named. It is now B, book, no instead of catalog only.
- **"Eric's own" not supported (1):** 17561e96, "IA Assessment Manual". I set it to B, atomize, no. It stays off the shortlist either way; the change is from catalog only to atomize. See the claim check below.
- **Duplicate kept the worse copy (2 rows, outside the 94):** Legacy (James Kerr) holds its candidacy on 1giYj6vw, which is a 0-byte file. That row was a "keep" in round 1. I moved candidacy to the real 163-page copy 080e99ed (B, book, yes) and set the 0-byte copy to B, catalog only, no. 4b25e110 is a second real copy (163 pages, 2.1 MB), so either real copy works.

**Reviewer claims**

- **Chris Ruf is Baylor staff: confirmed.** His title slide reads "Director of Athletics Performance – Olympic Sports Baylor University". Calling the talk "Baylor-internal" is wrong framing, though. It is a public 2019 Trinity conference talk, and rule 4 covers Eric's own work, not a colleague's. I still accept B, atomize, no because a 21-page career-lessons talk is not a candidate on its merits. Skodinski is the same case: her Baylor link is only inferred from the matching title format and the same Trinity 2019 folder, and her label stands.
- **"IA Assessment Manual" is Eric's own: not shown.** It sits in a playbook folder with a BAYLOR VERSION (Eric's own AP Assessment Manual drafts) and a CLEMSON VERSION (Clemson's playbook, kept as a reference). There is also a "University of Iowa Sports Performance Assessment Manual - DRAFT.pdf" in Literature & Textbooks. Eric may have worked at Iowa (an "Iowa basecamp" folder of 2017 lifting files), so it could be an internal document from a past job. It is not a candidate under either reading.
- **"Legacy" (James Kerr) is 0 bytes: true for that copy only.** Two real copies exist, so the fix is to move the candidacy, not drop it.

**The dropped candidates you asked me to weigh**

- **CSCS study material and USAW Level 1 manual:** I agree with dropping them, though these are the closest calls. Both are baseline certification content most S&C staff already know. Neither would change how a football staff trains. B, book is the right label for both.
- **Female British basketball report:** I agree. It is a single thesis study (139 pages, no text layer), and paper to Zotero fits.

**Other checks**

- The Hawkin force plate guide, Winkelman deck, Rolf, Stone and Mann rows correctly switched from book or paper to atomize.
- No route breaks the 80-page book rule.
- Every "already in Zotero" row has a verified or skipped_existing_pdf status.
- The 11 rows moved from C skip to B catalog only "name only:" follow rule 2.
- The other duplicate fixes kept the better copy: The System (the 385-page, 13.7 MB copy is kept), Kraemer, the Yessis Part I/II sizes add up (2 + 6 = 8 pages), and the 65-page Stone deck is kept.
- One reason is wrong but the label stands: the Charlie Francis row (2da88834) points to 0627e5e7 as "Vancouver seminar notes", but that key is Dan John's From the Ground Up.
- Out of scope, not written: 1OQA9rz1, a 0-byte copy of The System, is labelled B atomize and should be catalog only.

**Verdict on round 1: GO AFTER FIXES.** The review was careful and mostly right, but it was a little too harsh on named practitioner books and wrongly treated a colleague's public talk as internal. Apply the 6 rows above.
